use-after-free: Move the final read before cleanup, or extend the lifetime so cleanup happens after every user has finished. Follow the release note: freeing an alias invalidates the original pointer too. Assigning NULL to one variable does not repair other dangling aliases. An error means the object is released on every path to the use; a warning ("may have been freed") means some paths release it, so make the release and the use agree on every path. See [your first check](/getting-started/first-check/).
double-free: Give each allocation one clear cleanup path. After ownership transfer, let the new owner release it. On error paths, track whether ownership actually transferred before local cleanup. Reference-counted objects need one release per acquired share.
use-after-move: Stop using the old owning pointer after transfer. Borrow the object when the callee only needs temporary access, or use a new value returned by the operation. With realloc, distinguish success from failure and avoid keeping aliases into the old storage after successful growth.
conflicting-borrow: Delay release, transfer, or mutation until the borrow's final use, or shorten the borrow by moving its last use earlier. A warning means the conflict exists on some paths only; restructure so every path releases the object after the borrow ends.
lifetime-too-short: Ensure the referent lives at least as long as every pointer that escapes. Return a value, use caller-provided storage, or allocate storage with an ownership contract instead of returning an address into a local stack frame.
unsafe-operation: Inspect why the pointer or call is raw. Prefer a modeled or verified interface with an accurate contract. If the operation necessarily crosses the supported model, put the smallest reviewed operation inside a WEAVEC_UNSAFE boundary and document the assumptions. Unsafe code still affects ownership outside the boundary.
mismatched-release: Pair the resource with its allocator's release family: malloc with free, fopen with fclose, and opendir with closedir. For a custom family, express the contract with WEAVEC_OWNED and WEAVEC_OWNED_BY and ensure wrapper bodies agree.
leak: Release or transfer the owned resource on every applicable exit path. Before overwriting an owning pointer, dispose of the old resource. Free owned child allocations before their container. A shared cleanup label can make C error paths easier to audit.
null-dereference: Check nullable results before their first use and keep that condition on every path reaching the dereference. The error means the pointer is null on every path from a non-allocator source. A pointer that may be null is not reported: weavec-cc checks it at run time instead. Propagate allocation or lookup failure to callers when appropriate. Use WEAVEC_NONNULL only for an interface whose callers can establish the requirement.
use-of-uninitialized: Initialize the pointer or record field on every path before reading it. A declaration alone does not establish a value. The error means no path assigns it first. Pointers that may be uninitialized are zero-initialized in the enforcing modes, so their dereference is checked at run time instead of reported.
invalid-release: Release the original allocation base with the correct releaser. Stack objects, string literals, and interior pointers are not independently freeable. Keep the owning base separate from traversal cursors.
out-of-bounds: Compare the access against the actual allocation size, including element size and space for string terminators. Array indices must be smaller than the element count. Establish and preserve bounds across calls; a capacity field does not enlarge the allocation it describes. The error means the access fails for every value the analysis allows against an exact extent; an access that only may overrun is checked at run time instead.
invalid-integer-operation: Validate operands before the operation: divisors must be nonzero, shifts must have valid counts, signed results must be representable, and VLA dimensions must be positive. Check multiplication and conversion before using a result as an allocation size. See [integers and bounds](/guides/integers-and-bounds/).
annotation-mismatch: Compare the annotation with the function body and its callers. Correct the implementation or the declared contract so they describe the same ownership, extent, and effects. Do not strengthen an annotation simply to silence a diagnostic.
invalid-annotation: Check the macro spelling, placement, supported declaration kind, and named parameters or fields. WEAVEC_COUNTED_BY and WEAVEC_SIZED_BY must name a sibling integer parameter or field, WEAVEC_ENDED_BY a sibling pointer, and WEAVEC_OWNED_BY requires WEAVEC_OWNED. See [annotation placement](/reference/annotation-placement/).
contradicted-assumption: The assumption is false on the path the note describes, so the program would trap there. Fix the code that makes the value violate the assumption, or correct the assumption to what the code guarantees. Do not weaken an assumption only to silence the error; an assumption the analysis cannot decide is checked at run time instead.
allocation-failure: Test the allocation's result before its first use and handle the failure, for example by returning an error or calling an abort routine. The warning is off by default because the enforcing modes already trap on the null dereference; enable it to find the places that should report the failure gracefully.
unresolved-operation: Read the reason: it names what the analysis could not establish, such as an unknown extent or a callee that may free the pointer. Give the operation a checkable bound, for example by passing the length with WEAVEC_COUNTED_BY, give the callee an ownership annotation, or add its definition to the program. When a spatial or null operation is correct for reasons WeaveC cannot see, isolate it in a reviewed WEAVEC_UNSAFE region; its facets are then trusted and listed in the ledger.
unchecked-operation: The operation is safe only because of a runtime check, which -fweavec-require=proven does not accept. Establish the fact statically, for example by testing the pointer, bounding the index, or declaring the parameter WEAVEC_NONNULL where every caller can guarantee it, or use -fweavec-require=checked to accept the check.
unanalyzed-input: Build the named inputs with weavec-cc so each object carries its WeaveC record, and rebuild objects whose record is stale. Archives and shared libraries do not carry records yet; calls into them are trusted, and the ledger lists them. Disable the warning with -Wno-weavec-unanalyzed-input only for inputs that are reviewed or out of scope.
